questions.question: GDP calculated at some constant set of prices is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**real GDP.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Real GDP** is calculated by **adjusting nominal GDP **for** inflation**, which gives a more accurate measure of **economic growth.**
 
• Real GDP is used to compare** economic growth over time**, as it reflects changes in the quantity of **goods and services **produced rather than changes in prices.
 
• **Domestic GDP** is a measure of the value of all goods and services produced within a **country's borders,** regardless of the nationality of the producers.
 
• **Current GDP** refers to the most recent measurement of a** country's GDP,** regardless of the prices used to calculate it.
 
• **Nominal GDP** is calculated using **current prices** and does not account for **inflation, **which can lead to an overestimation of economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GDP** stands for **Gross Domestic Product** and is a measure of the **total value of goods and services **produced within a country's borders.
 
• **Real GDP** is considered a more accurate measure of economic growth because it adjusts for inflation, which can distort the** value of goods and services produced.**
 
• **Domestic GDP** is often used in conjunction with other measures, such as **Gross National Product (GNP)**, which includes the value of goods and services produced by a country's citizens, regardless of where they are located.
 
• **Current GDP **is useful for** tracking short-term changes **in the economy, but it may not provide an accurate picture of long-term trends.
 
• **Nominal GDP** is often used to compare the** economic size of different countries or regions**, but it can be misleading if prices are not taken into account.

questions.question: Duties levied on goods produced within the country are ___________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**excise taxes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Excise taxes:-**

 
 
• These are levied on goods produced within the country for domestic consumption.
 
• These taxes are imposed at the manufacturing stage and are included in the price of the product.
 
• Excise taxes are different from customs duties which are levied on goods imported into the country.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anti-dumping taxes:-**

 
 
• These are imposed on imported goods that are sold at prices lower than their normal value in the exporting country to protect the domestic industry. 
 
 
 
• **Wealth taxes:-**
 
 
• These are levied on the net wealth of individuals or companies and are not related to the production or sale of goods
 
 
 
• **Custom duties:-**
 
 
• These are taxes imposed on goods that are imported into the country from foreign nations. They are also known as import duties or tariffs.

questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana was launched in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2000**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY) was launched by the Indian government in the year 2000.
 
• This scheme was initiated to focus on the village development in five critical areas - primary health, primary education, housing, rural roads, and drinking water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The primary objective of PMGY is to achieve the goal of sustainable human development at the village level.
 
• Primary Health: The scheme provides for health centers and necessary healthcare infrastructure at the village level. 
 
• Primary Education: Under PMGY, the government allocates resources for strengthening the primary education system in rural areas, including the establishment of new schools and providing necessary infrastructure and learning materials.
 
• Housing: PMGY also aims to improve the housing condition of the rural poor.
 
• Rural Roads: PMGY recognizes the importance of connectivity for the overall development of villages.
 
• Drinking Water: Under the scheme, the government provides resources to ensure the supply of safe and clean drinking water to the rural population.
 
• The funds for this centrally sponsored scheme are shared between the central government and the states. 
 
• The success of PMGY depends on the active participation of the community in the planning and implementation of the programs.

questions.question: To which of the following sectors of the economy do Basel Ill norms belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Banking.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Basel Norms:**

 
 
• Basel norms are the** international banking regulations to strengthen the international banking system.**
 
• It is in the form of an agreement by the Basel Committee of Banking supervision which mainly focuses on the risk to banks and the financial system.
 
 
 
• **Basel-I norms:**
 
 
• Basel, I was introduced in 1988 and focused on credit risk.
 
• India adopted Basel 1 guidelines in 1999 as it defines the capital and structure of risk weights for banks.
 
• The minimum Capital requirement was fixed at 8% of risk-weighted assets.
 
 
 
• **Basel-Il norms:**
 
 
• Basel II norms were established in 2000 and were based on three parameters capital adequacy requirement, supervisory requirement, and market discipline.
 
• A minimum capital adequacy requirement of 8% of risk-weighted assets was fixed.
 
 
 
• **Basel-Ill norms**:
 
 
• Basel III norms were issued in 2010 as a response to the financial crisis of 2008.
 
• It aims to promote a resilient banking system by focusing on capital leverage funding and liquidity.
 
• The capital adequacy ratio was fixed at 12.9%.
 
• The leverage rate was fixed at 3%.
 
• Banks' strength was improved Liquidity Coverage Ratio and Net Stable Fund Rate.

questions.question: Due to rapid urbanisation, the human lifestyle has changed severely; obesity is a major health issue in such condition. Which of the following is a reason for obesity?

options.text: Excessive intake of high calorie foods
Lack of vitamins in regular diet

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Excessive intake of high calorie foods**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Excessive intake of high calorie foods** is a primary reason for obesity, especially in rapidly urbanizing areas.
 
• Urbanization often leads to lifestyle changes that include increased consumption of fast food, sugary beverages, and other high-calorie, low-nutrient foods.
 
• This dietary shift, combined with reduced physical activity, contributes significantly to weight gain and obesity.
 
• Obesity is associated with various health issues such as diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and hypertension.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Obesity is defined as having a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher.
 
• Urban environments often provide less opportunity for physical activity due to sedentary jobs and limited access to recreational areas.
 
• Public health initiatives aimed at reducing obesity often focus on promoting healthier eating habits and increasing physical activity.
 
• Other factors contributing to obesity include genetics, metabolism, behavior, and culture.
 
• Addressing obesity requires a multifaceted approach including education, policy changes, and community support.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines transfer payments?

options.text: Payments made to individuals in exchange for their labour or services
Payments made by the government to individuals without any corresponding production of goods or services
Payments made by businesses to their shareholders as a share of profits
Payments made by individuals to the government in the form of taxes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Payments made by the government to individuals without any corresponding production of goods or services.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Transfer payments refer to the sums of money distributed by the government to individuals without any goods or services being provided in return.
 
• These payments are essentially financial transfers from the government's funds to individuals, aiming to redistribute income and provide social benefits.Examples of transfer payments include unemployment benefits, welfare payments, and social security.
 
• Unlike taxes or purchases, these payments do not directly contribute to any economic production but are critical for supporting individuals who may be in need or less fortunate, thus maintaining economic stability and supporting social welfare

questions.question: Which Bill was passed in the Parliament in 2022 to authorise payment certain sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of India for the services of the financial year 2022-23?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Appropriation Bill.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Appropriation Bill **was passed in the** **Parliament in 2022 to authorise payment of certain sums from and out of the **Consolidated Fund of India** for the services of the financial year **2022-23.**
 
• **The Appropriation Bill is a money bill that authorizes the government to withdraw funds from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet its expenditures during the financial year.**
 
• It is introduced in the Parliament after the presentation of the **Union Budget.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Finance Bill is also a money bill that deals with the government's revenue and expenditure proposals for the upcoming financial year. **
 
• The Electricity (Amendment) Bill is a non-money bill that seeks to amend the Electricity Act, 2003 to bring about reforms in the power sector, including the promotion of renewable energy and the introduction of competition in the distribution segment.
 
• **The Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Bill is also a non-money bill that seeks to amend the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 to provide for better protection of wildlife and their habitats in India.**

questions.question: If we deduct depreciation from GNP the measure of aggregate income that we obtain is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Net National Product.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net National Product (NNP)** is calculated by subtracting **depreciation** from **Gross National Product (GNP)**.
 
• **Depreciation **refers to the** decrease in the value of an asset **over time due to **wear and tear or obsolescence.**
 
• NNP is frequently assessed annually as a way to gauge how well a country is **maintaining minimum production standards**.
 
• Although NNP is frequently used in environmental economics, Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the method that is most frequently used to assess **national income and economic prosperity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP) **is the total value of all **goods and services** produced within a country's borders in a given period, regardless of ownership.
 
• **National Income** is the sum of all incomes earned by **individuals and businesses** within a country's borders in a given period, including wages, profits, and rent.
 
• **Private Income **is the income earned by individuals within a** country's borders **in a given period, including wages, salaries, and dividends.

questions.question: What is a prominent trend in the microfinance sector in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Integration of mobile banking services**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Integration of mobile banking services** is a prominent trend in the microfinance sector in India.
 
• Mobile banking services are being increasingly adopted to enhance accessibility and convenience for microfinance clients.
 
• This trend is helping to streamline operations, reduce costs, and improve the efficiency of financial transactions in the microfinance sector.
 
• The use of mobile banking services is particularly beneficial in rural and remote areas, where traditional banking infrastructure may be limited.
 
• It also supports financial inclusion by providing underserved populations with easier access to financial services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microfinance** refers to financial services provided to low-income individuals or those who do not have access to typical banking services.
 
• The sector has seen significant growth in India, driven by the need to promote financial inclusion and support small-scale entrepreneurs.
 
• Technological advancements, such as mobile banking, play a crucial role in transforming the microfinance landscape.
 
• Mobile banking services include features like mobile wallets, SMS banking, and mobile apps, which facilitate various financial transactions such as deposits, withdrawals, and fund transfers.
 
• Regulatory support and initiatives by the government and financial institutions have further accelerated the adoption of mobile banking in the microfinance sector.

questions.question: In the context of microfinance, what does ‘S’ stand for in SHG?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Self**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** are informal associations of people who choose to come together to find ways to improve their living conditions.
 
• They are usually composed of 10-20 members, often women, from similar socio-economic backgrounds.
 
• The primary objective of SHGs is to enhance the socio-economic conditions of their members through collective efforts and mutual support.
 
• SHGs play a crucial role in financial inclusion by enabling members to pool their savings, access credit, and engage in income-generating activities.
 
• SHGs are a key component of microfinance initiatives, providing a platform for the delivery of financial services to the underserved and marginalized sections of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microfinance**

 
 
• Microfinance refers to the provision of financial services to low-income individuals or groups who typically lack access to traditional banking services.
 
• It includes a range of services such as microcredit, savings, insurance, and remittances.
 
• Microfinance aims to promote financial inclusion and empower economically disadvantaged people.
 
• It has been recognized as a powerful tool for poverty alleviation and socio-economic development.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion**
 
 
• Financial inclusion involves ensuring that individuals and businesses have access to useful and affordable financial products and services.
 
• These services should meet their needs and be delivered responsibly and sustainably.
 
• Financial inclusion is essential for reducing poverty, fostering economic growth, and promoting social equity.
 
 
 
• **Women Empowerment through SHGs**
 
 
• SHGs have been instrumental in empowering women by enhancing their financial independence and decision-making power.
 
• Participation in SHGs helps women develop skills, confidence, and a sense of solidarity.
 
• Empowered women contribute to the well-being of their families and communities, leading to broader social and economic development.
 
 
 
• **Government Support for SHGs**
 
 
• The Indian government, through various schemes and programs, supports the formation and strengthening of SHGs.
 
• Initiatives like the National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM) aim to promote SHGs and enhance their capacity.
 
• Government support includes financial assistance, training, and capacity-building activities for SHG members.
